report.source_text: He was born at term following an uncomplicated antenatal period and had a normal perinatal period without episodes of hypoglycemia or circulatory collapse. He was the only child of a pair of consanguineous parents. His growth parameters at birth were within normal limits; weight 3.3 kg (at median for age), length 50 cm (at median for age), and head circumference 35 cm (between median and +1 SD). Since birth his growth chart demonstrated accelerated growth in weight, length, and head circumference (Fig. 2). His parents observed hyperpigmentation at birth which worsened gradually over time. His developmental history revealed marginal gross motor developmental delay; at 10 months of age, he was able to sit without support, however, he was unable to come to seated position on his own, stand with support, or crawl. His vision, fine motor, speech, and social development milestones were age appropriate. There were no previous hospital admissions, recurrent infections, seizures, episodes of shock, or documented hypoglycemia.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old Sri Lankan boy born to consanguineous parents presented with generalized hyperpigmentation (observed at birth, worsening gradually), progressive overgrowth (accelerated growth in weight, length, and head circumference since birth), and marginal gross motor developmental delay. Physical examination documented tall stature (length 84 cm >+3 SD, weight 12.6 kg +3 SD, head circumference 48 cm +2 SD) with hyperpigmentation involving oral mucosa, palms, and soles. Laboratory investigations revealed isolated glucocorticoid deficiency: very low serum cortisol (<22 nmol/l, basal <4.39 nmol/L), markedly elevated ACTH (>1734 pg/ml), and normal serum aldosterone. ACTH stimulation testing confirmed severe primary glucocorticoid deficiency with no cortisol response to synthetic ACTH at 30 and 60 minutes. Glucocorticoid replacement therapy was initiated, with documented clinical response at 5 months showing decreased pigmentation and slowing of growth velocity. The clinical presentation of isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with hyperpigmentation, tall stature, and autosomal recessive inheritance pattern (consanguineous parents) is diagnostic of FGD.
